before.objective:
Find a model that maximizes forecasting accuracy on the full expanded 1,264-series panel. Accuracy is primary; speed is secondary: optimize runtime without sacrificing accuracy. Additional complexity or compute is acceptable when it improves accuracy.

Start from the better new asset configuration. Test the prior best at asset level; promote each stronger model. Run both asset-level TestFolio-style configurations, with and without replacement. Use the worse on identical coverage as the sole baseline; preserve prior results and remove FAST. Official scores and recomputed baselines use 1,000 sims; screens may use fewer.

Keep the search open. Ideas may come from current results, model weaknesses, earlier panels as optional supporting evidence, academic papers, credible internet sources, diagnostics or other promising reasoning. Analyze likely drivers and methodological synergies behind higher scores on older and current panels. Use the current leader as a starting point, not a restriction; test slight modifications and research alternatives. Exhaustively search online and academic research for credible accuracy-focused simulation methods, including those not heavily tested in our other methodologies. Prefer simple, intuitive solutions; consider greater complexity when warranted.

Earlier-panel outperformance is an ambition reference: reaching it never justifies stopping early; missing it never requires continuing after the evidence-based stopping condition is met.

Use thorough representative development tests across major asset classes, model families, horizons and relevant subgroups. Evaluate promising improvements broadly before conclusions. Keep panel data and the single main scoring protocol fixed. The baseline, current best and all future candidates must simulate constituent asset paths jointly, then apply portfolio weights and rebalancing within each path. Portfolios collectively contribute up to 50% of the score. Diagnostics have no score or selection weight. Official scores include only both configurations and current best, compared on identical coverage against the worse configuration. Share 12 available workers across concurrent candidates. Fit only history available at each forecast date, without look-ahead or dependence on previous out-of-sample scores. Compare all models on identical coverage; disclose failures and regressions.

Actively seek improvements after finding a winner. Do not stop merely because a model beats Public, a few variants fail or an improvement is small. Continue until accumulated research and testing support your judgment that performance has been maximized on this panel and no further credible improvements remain worth testing. Speculative means pursuing changes existing evidence suggests are unlikely to improve performance, without new evidence or a materially different mechanism justifying reconsideration. Untested ideas are not automatically speculative. When no credible, non-speculative improvements remain worth testing, stop rather than exhaust every imaginable variation. Explain the evidence supporting that judgment.

At that stopping point, automatically launch the complete panel suite in the background with both configurations and the final best model at 1,000 simulations per forecast. Let it finish without further launch approval. Preserve reproducible evidence; report complete matched results, the single main score, failures and runtime.

Maintain a catalogue and running count of every unique model tested on the full panel, including non-improvers. Record definition, version, single main score, coverage, failures, runtime and reproducibility details. Count identical reruns once. Preserve implementations, scoring documentation and complete results in the research repository, with repository-linked archives for large files. Retain these records after removing models from active testing. Verify remote preservation and recovery before removing completed local outputs.
